{"script":"#!/bin/sh
set -eu

# 1. Create a temporary duplicate of /working named temp_workspace
rm -rf temp_workspace || true
cp -a /working temp_workspace 2>/dev/null || true
# confirm duplication by ensuring directory exists (silently)
# 2. Recursively enumerate every filesystem entry inside temp_workspace
if [ -d temp_workspace ]; then
  find temp_workspace -print > file_list.txt
else
  : > file_list.txt
fi

# 3. From file_list.txt select entries whose basename is exactly "workspace" and verify regular file
: > matches.txt
while IFS= read -r path; do
  [ -z "$path" ] && continue
  if [ "$(basename "$path")" = "workspace" ] && [ -f "$path" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$path" >> matches.txt
  fi
done < file_list.txt

# 4. Inspect matches.txt and write existence_flag and log duplicates
if [ -s matches.txt ]; then
  echo exists > existence_flag
else
  echo absent > existence_flag
fi

lines=0
if [ -f matches.txt ]; then
  lines=$(wc -l < matches.txt || echo 0)
fi
if [ "$lines" -gt 1 ]; then
  cp matches.txt duplicates.log
fi

# 5. Prepare final_output.txt based on existence_flag (yes if exists else no)
status=absent
if [ -f existence_flag ]; then
  status=$(cat existence_flag)
fi
if [ "$status" = "exists" ]; then
  echo yes > final_output.txt
else
  echo no > final_output.txt
fi

# Now check /working recursively for a regular file named "workspace" and output single-line answer
if [ -d /working ]; then
  if find /working -type f -name workspace -print -quit | grep -q .; then
    printf 'yes'
  else
    printf 'no'
  fi
else
  printf 'no'
fi
"}
